subject: Trifecta regional pool sizing + deal anchor for OrionAI
messages:
From: Elaine Park <elaine@orion.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: OrionAI Ops <ops@orion.ai>
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 08:12:00 -0800
Subject: Initial ask: regional pool sizing for Q1 pilot (APAC + EU + US)

Hi Hannah,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team liked the latency profile and the KV cache options. We were asked to share a short, high-level ask so procurement can start carving capacity into our Q1 plan. Top line: we need a dedicated inference footprint aligned to three regions (APAC, EU, US) for a 3-month pilot, with the option to convert to a longer committed capacity if numbers look good.

Quick numbers (estimates from our product/ops):
- APAC: 12 peak concurrent sessions, avg request length ~900 tokens, model: 7B quantized (preferred), burstable to 24 concurrent for peak events
- EU: 8 peak concurrent, avg 700 tokens, model: 7B quantized
- US: 16 peak concurrent, avg 1,200 tokens, model: 13B quantized for higher-quality reranking

Attached is a traffic forecast CSV and a short note on SLAs they require. Can you propose region-specific pool sizing (GPU counts/types), a tentative commit level, and any immediate blockers (eg: KMS, network, region availability)? We need something we can show to procurement by EOW.

Appreciate it — Elaine

--
Elaine Park
Head of Platform Operations, OrionAI
elaine@orion.ai

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Park <elaine@orion.ai>
Cc: OrionAI Ops <ops@orion.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Initial ask: regional pool sizing for Q1 pilot (APAC + EU + US)

Elaine — thanks for the detailed numbers and the CSV. Karthik and I reviewed quickly and have a short action plan below. We can get a draft SOW and an anchor commit for procurement by Friday, but need two clarifications to finalize sizing:

1) Tail-latency SLO: do you need 99th percentile token latency under 250ms for all regions, or is us/eu only (apac can be relaxed to 350ms during bursts)?
2) Data residency + KMS: is there an existing KMS/HSM arrangement you want us to use in EU and APAC, or should we plan for Redwood-managed keys initially?

Preliminary recommendation (fast-pass numbers to share with procurement):
- APAC: 6x A10G equivalent nodes (continuous baseline) with 2x burst nodes; supports 12 sustained concurrents and headroom for bursts to 24 with pre-warm.
- EU: 4x A10G equivalent nodes baseline, 1x burst node.
- US: 8x A10G (or mixed 80% A10G + 20% H100 L29 for 13B inference) baseline, 4x burst nodes.

These map to an initial committed tranche that covers baseline capacity for the 3-month pilot with burst billing for the extras. We'll draft an SOW with explicit scaling/fallback policies (canary -> full cutover -> fallback to smaller model variant).

I'll loop Karthik (deal lead) and Olga (sourcing) to confirm availability in target regions and runway for reserved capacity. If procurement needs a conservative commit number, propose "baseline + 20%" of the peak concurrency as anchor to avoid repeated resizing during the pilot.

I can follow up with a short mutual action plan doc and the SOW draft.

Best,
Hannah

--
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Internal: OrionAI tri-region commit ask — availability + pricing guidance

Team — forwarding Elaine's forecast and my reply. Short asks: can sourcing confirm APAC/EU availability (A10G class) for early Jan start? Rishi, need a quick cost sketch for two flavors: committed baseline (3-month) and a baseline+burst pricing model.

Suggested sizing (from my note to them):
- APAC baseline: 6 nodes (A10G-eq), 2 burst nodes
- EU baseline: 4 nodes, 1 burst
- US baseline: 8 nodes (mix), 4 burst

Key constraints to surface to the customer if we don't have availability: pre-warm latency will increase, can mitigate with model variant (7B -> 3B for ephemeral spikes) but that affects output quality. Also note KMS options — if customer wants customer-managed keys we need to schedule a KMS onboarding step per region (adds 7–10 business days).

Olga — can you confirm a rough ETA for procurement/commit pricing and whether we can hold a partial tranche for them while they finalize SOW?

Thanks — Hannah

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 13:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Internal: OrionAI tri-region commit ask — availability + pricing guidance

Quick update — I checked capacity in our inventory and here's what we can promise for a Jan start:
- APAC: A10G-class nodes available to reserve: 18 (we can allocate 8 to Orion for pilot if needed)
- EU: A10G-class nodes available: 10 (4 reserved ok)
- US: H100 L29 inventory constrained for large sustained 13B; we have more A10G equivalents. If Orion insists on H100 for US, lead time is ~6 weeks to source; recommend hybrid baseline (A10G) + one H100 node for heavy tails.

Pricing sketch for 3-month pilot (rounded):
- Baseline (committed): APAC baseline 6 nodes = $X/month (I'll send detailed sheet).
- Burst pricing: 2x baseline burst nodes billed at on-demand uplift.

I can hold APAC/EU baseline nodes on a 7-day reservation while they finalize SOW. For KMS: we can provision Redwood-managed keys in APAC/EU immediately; customer-managed KMS requires paperwork that will push start by ~10 business days.

I'll attach a short spreadsheet with line items (see attachments).

- Olga

--
Olga Petrov
Head of Sourcing, Redwood Inference

From: Elaine Park <elaine@orion.ai>

Date: Thu, 2 Dec 2026 14:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Initial ask: regional pool sizing for Q1 pilot (APAC + EU + US)

Hannah / Karthik — thanks, this is super helpful. Procurement is happy to proceed with baseline+20% anchor for their approval cycle. They prefer Redwood-managed KMS to avoid onboarding delays. Please send the draft SOW and the mutual action plan; procurement wants the SOW, anchor commit, and the traffic forecast attached.

Next step: can we lock APAC/EU baseline reserve today (7-day hold) and schedule a brief tech sync with your infra team Thursday 11am PT? We'll share a list of test prompts and a short perf checklist.

Once we have the SOW I can route to procurement — Elaine

--
Elaine Park
Head of Platform Operations, OrionAI
